text: Given your age and symptoms, I need to rule out Giant Cell Arteritis. Do you have jaw claudication (pain when chewing) or scalp tenderness? REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP

speaker: Doctor
text: Since inflammatory markers are normal, Giant Cell Arteritis is less likely, so I need to evaluate for other causes of progressive vision loss and headache. speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI is normal, I need to examine the back of your eyes to check for optic nerve swelling. REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the progressive vision loss, headache, and normal neuroimaging, I need to evaluate for a compressive lesion not fully captured by the initial MRI or an inflammatory process affecting the optic nerve. REQUEST TEST: CT Orbit with contrast

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the progressive vision loss, headache, and normal imaging/inflammatory markers, the most likely diagnosis is compressive optic neuropathy from a pituitary macroadenoma that may have been missed or is subtle, or potentially an atypical presentation of idiopathic intracranial hypertension. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pituitary Macroadenoma
